github-actions-s1.1-02.reason: ambiguous: after a first run, the REST API or gh can dispatch a workflow that exists only on a feature branch, so the claim is limited to the UI button (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.1-02.statement: The GitHub UI offers Run workflow for a workflow file that is on a feature branch and absent from the default branch.
github-actions-s1.1-02.explanation: The Run workflow button appears when the workflow file is on the default branch. After a first run, the REST API or GitHub CLI can dispatch it against another branch or tag.
github-actions-s1.1-02.misconception: Choosing a feature branch in the UI lifts the default-branch requirement for the Run workflow button.

github-actions-s1.1-09.reason: weak_card: name giveaway; replaced with the verifier's secrets: inherit fact because a second drop would take 1.1 below 9 (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.1-09.statement: secrets: inherit passes secrets to a called workflow in another organization of the same enterprise.
github-actions-s1.1-09.explanation: inherit passes every secret the caller can reach, including organization, repository and environment secrets, to a called workflow in the same organization or enterprise.

github-actions-s1.2-01.reason: weak_card: needs is a name giveaway; replaced with the always() exception because 1.2 already drops s1.2-10 (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.2-01.statement: A job that needs a failed job still runs when its own if condition uses always().
github-actions-s1.2-01.explanation: A failed or skipped needs dependency normally skips the dependent job; always() in jobs.<job_id>.if lets it run regardless of that result.

github-actions-s1.2-04.reason: weak_card: ::warning is a name giveaway; replaced with stop-commands because 1.2 already drops s1.2-10 (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.2-04.statement: After ::stop-commands::TOKEN, the runner ignores workflow commands until a step echoes ::TOKEN::.
github-actions-s1.2-04.explanation: stop-commands pauses workflow command processing so a step can print text such as a script without running it as commands; echoing the same unique token resumes processing.

github-actions-s1.2-07.reason: explanation_error: include is added to every combination it does not conflict with; it creates a new combination only when it fits none (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.2-07.statement: A matrix include entry that conflicts with an original axis value overwrites that original combination.
github-actions-s1.2-07.explanation: include adds its keys to every combination it does not conflict with; only an entry that fits no combination becomes a new one. Original matrix values are never overwritten.
github-actions-s1.2-07.misconception: An include entry replaces an original matrix variant when its axis value conflicts.

github-actions-s1.2-08.reason: weak_card: max-parallel is a name giveaway; replaced with the default parallelism behaviour (the verifier's 'Without' was reworded to avoid a negation) (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.2-08.statement: With strategy.max-parallel unset, GitHub runs as many matrix jobs at once as runners allow.
github-actions-s1.2-08.explanation: GitHub maximizes parallel matrix jobs based on available runners; strategy.max-parallel caps how many of a matrix's jobs run at the same time.

github-actions-s1.3-03.reason: weak_card: the steps.<job> distractor is invented; replaced with the realistic jobs vs needs context confusion because 1.3 already drops s1.3-09 (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.3-03.statement: A dependent job reads a needed job's declared outputs through the jobs.<job_id>.outputs context.
github-actions-s1.3-03.explanation: A job that lists another job in needs reads that job's declared outputs through needs.<job_id>.outputs.<output_name>.
github-actions-s1.3-03.misconception: The jobs context exposes job outputs to dependent jobs in any workflow.

github-actions-s1.3-07.reason: weak_card: name giveaway; replaced with the download-all behaviour because 1.3 already drops s1.3-09 (appliesTo: actions/download-artifact v5, the version the docs page uses) (final: keep)
github-actions-s1.3-07.statement: Omitting name in actions/download-artifact fetches all of the run's artifacts, one folder per artifact.
github-actions-s1.3-07.explanation: Omitting name makes the action download all artifacts uploaded in the current workflow run, creating a directory named after each artifact.

source.title: Store and share data with workflow artifacts

github-actions-s2.1-02.reason: weak_card: truism by arithmetic; replaced with include-after-exclude because 2.1 already drops s2.1-04 (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.1-02.statement: A matrix include entry restores a job combination that the same matrix's exclude list had removed.
github-actions-s2.1-02.explanation: GitHub processes all include combinations after exclude, so an include entry that matches an excluded combination adds that job back to the matrix.

github-actions-s2.1-05.reason: weak_card: name giveaway; replaced with the fail-fast and continue-on-error interaction because 2.1 already drops s2.1-04 (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.1-05.statement: A failing matrix job set to continue-on-error: true makes fail-fast cancel its sibling jobs.
github-actions-s2.1-05.explanation: A matrix job with continue-on-error: true can fail while the other matrix jobs keep running; fail-fast cancels in-progress and queued jobs when a job with continue-on-error: false fails.
github-actions-s2.1-05.misconception: fail-fast cancels the matrix whenever any job fails, whatever its continue-on-error setting.

github-actions-s2.2-05.reason: weak_card: truism; replaced with the sign-in requirement because 2.2 already drops s2.2-02 (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.2-05.statement: Viewing a public repository's workflow runs requires a GitHub sign-in.
github-actions-s2.2-05.explanation: Even for public repositories, GitHub shows workflow run information, such as run status and logs, only to people logged in to a GitHub account.

github-actions-s2.2-06.reason: weak_card: -n NAME is a name giveaway; replaced with the cross-run download because 2.2 already drops s2.2-02 (appliesTo: actions/download-artifact v5) (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.2-06.statement: actions/download-artifact needs a token and run ID to fetch another run's artifact.
github-actions-s2.2-06.explanation: Artifacts from a different workflow or workflow run are fetched by supplying a token and the run identifier to the download-artifact action.

source.title: Store and share data with workflow artifacts

github-actions-s2.3-01.reason: weak_card: truism; replaced with the copy-independence fact the plan intended (study guide: 'copy scaffold, independent after creation') because 2.3 already drops s2.3-05 (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.3-01.statement: Editing an organization workflow template leaves workflows already created from it unchanged.
github-actions-s2.3-01.explanation: Choosing a template commits a copy of it as a new workflow file in the repository. For logic that should update centrally, the template can call a reusable workflow.

github-actions-s2.3-04.reason: explanation_error: the explanation stated the Read-access fact that s4.1-08 tests (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.3-04.statement: An internal `.github` repository offers its workflow templates to public repositories in the enterprise.
github-actions-s2.3-04.explanation: Templates from an internal .github repository are offered only to internal and private repositories. Only a public .github repository serves templates to every repository type.
github-actions-s2.3-04.misconception: Internal workflow templates are offered to public repositories.

github-actions-s2.3-10.reason: weak_card: name giveaway and near-paraphrase; replaced with fork schedule disabling ('by default' removed from the statement to avoid a true-only tell) because 2.3 already drops s2.3-05 (final: keep)
github-actions-s2.3-10.statement: GitHub disables the scheduled workflows in a new fork of a public repository.
github-actions-s2.3-10.explanation: When a public repository is forked, its scheduled workflows start disabled to prevent unneeded runs; the fork owner can enable them again from the Actions tab.

github-actions-s3.1-06.reason: ambiguous: in a container job the step runs inside the job container, not directly on the runner OS (final: keep)
github-actions-s3.1-06.statement: In a job that sets jobs.<job_id>.container, a JavaScript action step runs inside that job container.
github-actions-s3.1-06.explanation: jobs.<job_id>.container runs every step that names no container of its own inside the job container, so JavaScript actions execute there and not on the host.

github-actions-s3.1-07.reason: weak_card: generic exit-code truism; replaced with the Docker action USER rule (reworded as behaviour, not 'GitHub tells') because 3.1 already drops s3.1-09 (final: keep)
github-actions-s3.1-07.statement: A Docker container action whose Dockerfile switches to a non-root USER loses access to GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
github-actions-s3.1-07.explanation: Docker container actions must run as the default Docker user, root; a USER instruction in the Dockerfile cuts the action off from the GITHUB_WORKSPACE directory.

github-actions-s3.2-02.reason: weak_card: strawman on the meaning of 'default'; replaced with composite INPUT_ variables ('automatically' removed to avoid a false-only tell) because 3.2 already drops s3.2-06 (final: keep)
github-actions-s3.2-02.statement: A composite action's run steps read caller inputs from INPUT_<NAME> environment variables.
github-actions-s3.2-02.explanation: GitHub creates no INPUT_<NAME> variables for composite actions; their steps read caller values through the inputs context, for example ${{ inputs.name }}.
github-actions-s3.2-02.misconception: Composite actions receive inputs as INPUT_ environment variables like JavaScript and Docker actions.

github-actions-s3.2-05.reason: weak_card: name giveaway and near-copy; replaced with the post-if default because 3.2 already drops s3.2-06 (final: keep)
github-actions-s3.2-05.statement: A JavaScript action's post script runs after a later job step fails when post-if is unset.
github-actions-s3.2-05.explanation: post-if defaults to always(), and its status check functions read the job's status, so the action's cleanup runs even when later steps fail.

github-actions-s3.3-09.reason: weak_card: the word 'immutable' gives the answer away; replaced with future-only immutability (volatility may_change) because 3.3 already drops s3.3-06 (final: keep)
github-actions-s3.3-09.statement: Enabling release immutability on an action repository locks the assets of releases published before it was enabled.
github-actions-s3.3-09.explanation: Release immutability applies only to releases published after the setting is enabled; releases published earlier stay editable.
github-actions-s3.3-09.misconception: Turning on immutability retroactively locks existing releases.

github-actions-s3.3-10.reason: weak_card: name giveaway; replaced with reusable workflow ref updates because 3.3 already drops s3.3-06 (final: keep)
github-actions-s3.3-10.statement: Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem also bumps refs of reusable workflows called in workflows.
github-actions-s3.3-10.explanation: With package-ecosystem "github-actions", Dependabot keeps both action references and reusable workflows used inside workflows up to date, opening pull requests for outdated refs.

source.title: Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

github-actions-s4.2-04.reason: weak_card: definition card; replaced with the listener long poll because 4.2 already drops s4.2-10 (final: keep)
github-actions-s4.2-04.statement: ARC's runner scale set listener learns about queued jobs through an HTTPS long-poll connection to GitHub.
github-actions-s4.2-04.explanation: The listener pod authenticates to the GitHub Actions Service and holds an HTTPS long poll open until a Job Available message arrives, then scales the runners up.

github-actions-s4.2-05.reason: weak_card: strawman linking runner groups to the IP allow list; replaced with the hosted-runner requirement because 4.2 already drops s4.2-10 (Azure private networking also excludes standard hosted runners, so the false answer holds) (final: keep)
github-actions-s4.2-05.statement: An enterprise using an IP allow list can run its Actions jobs on standard GitHub-hosted runners.
github-actions-s4.2-05.explanation: With an IP allow list, Actions needs self-hosted runners or GitHub-hosted larger runners with static IP ranges, and admins add those runners' addresses to the allow list.
github-actions-s4.2-05.misconception: Standard hosted runners pass an enterprise IP allow list like any other GitHub traffic.

source.title: Restricting network traffic to your enterprise with an IP allow list

github-actions-s4.3-05.reason: weak_card: wording giveaway and the same access model as s4.3-01; replaced with vars in reusable workflows (s4.3-07 is the 4.3 drop) (final: keep)
github-actions-s4.3-05.statement: A reusable workflow's `vars` context reads the caller repository's variables.
github-actions-s4.3-05.explanation: A called workflow sees the configuration variables of the caller's repository; variables in the repository that stores the reusable workflow are not passed in.

github-actions-s5.1-04.reason: weak_card: wording tell and a changelog-only source; replaced with the rename case from the current OIDC reference (keeps may_change) (final: keep)
github-actions-s5.1-04.statement: Renaming a repository after July 15, 2026 leaves its OIDC `sub` claim in the name-only format.
github-actions-s5.1-04.explanation: Repositories created, renamed or transferred after July 15, 2026 use the immutable sub format with owner and repository IDs, such as repo:octo-org@123456/octo-repo@456789:ref:...
github-actions-s5.1-04.misconception: Only newly created repositories switch to the immutable subject format.

github-actions-s5.1-05.reason: weak_card: true by mechanics alone and never tests the injection point; replaced with expression substitution because 5.1 already drops s5.1-09 (final: keep)
github-actions-s5.1-05.statement: GitHub inserts `${{ }}` values into a `run` script before the shell runs, enabling script injection.
github-actions-s5.1-05.explanation: Expression values are pasted into the generated shell script, so an untrusted PR title can run as commands. Pass it through an intermediate env variable instead.

github-actions-s5.1-06.reason: ambiguous: the statement did not name the environment and could be read as a branch-protection review rule ('lets' removed to avoid a true-hedge tell) (final: fixed)
github-actions-s5.1-06.statement: One approval from a listed reviewer satisfies an environment's required-reviewer rule.
github-actions-s5.1-06.explanation: Only one of the listed users or teams has to approve; with Prevent self-review on, the user who started the deployment cannot be that approver. Other protection rules, such as a wait timer, still apply.

github-actions-s5.1-07.reason: weak_card: the name 'Prevent self-review' gives the answer away; replaced with the deployment branches confusion because 5.1 already drops s5.1-09 (final: keep)
github-actions-s5.1-07.statement: An environment's deployment branches and tags rule controls which users may approve its deployment jobs.
github-actions-s5.1-07.explanation: Deployment branches and tags restrict which branches or tags can deploy to the environment; approvers come from the required reviewers rule.
github-actions-s5.1-07.misconception: The deployment branches rule doubles as an approval list.

github-actions-s5.2-02.reason: weak_card: truism of hashing and a 1.3 topic; replaced with cache overage billing (volatility may_change) because 5.2 already drops s5.2-04 (final: fixed)
github-actions-s5.2-02.statement: GitHub bills a repository's extra cache storage only after its cache storage limit is set above the included allowance.
github-actions-s5.2-02.explanation: Each repository has an included cache allowance; GitHub charges for cache usage beyond it only when the repository's cache storage limit is configured higher than that allowance.

github-actions-s5.2-05.reason: weak_card: cancel-in-progress is a name giveaway; replaced with the default pending-run behaviour (volatility may_change: the queue property is new) because 5.2 already drops s5.2-04 (final: keep)
github-actions-s5.2-05.statement: With the default queue setting, a new run in a concurrency group cancels the run pending there.
github-actions-s5.2-05.explanation: A concurrency group holds one pending run by default, so the newer run replaces it. queue: max lets runs wait instead, and cancel-in-progress also cancels the running one.

source.title: Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs

github-actions-s5.2-06.reason: weak_card: timeout-minutes is a definition card; replaced with re-run billing (volatility may_change) because 5.2 already drops s5.2-04 (final: fixed)
github-actions-s5.2-06.statement: A re-run of a failed private-repository workflow on GitHub-hosted runners adds its minutes to the failed attempt's.
github-actions-s5.2-06.explanation: Minutes a failed attempt used stay counted: a workflow that fails after 5 minutes and then succeeds in a 10-minute re-run uses 15 minutes of the owner's allowance.

github-actions-s5.2-07.reason: out_of_scope: runner image stability belongs to 1.2/4.2 and overlaps s4.2-07; replaced with log storage billing (volatility may_change, appliesTo cleared) because 5.2 already drops s5.2-04 (final: keep)
github-actions-s5.2-07.statement: A run's log files and job summary count toward the repository owner's artifact storage allowance.
github-actions-s5.2-07.explanation: Logs and job summaries do not count as artifact storage; uploaded artifacts do, and they share one storage allowance with GitHub Packages.
github-actions-s5.2-07.misconception: Everything a workflow run stores is billed as artifact storage.

github-actions-s4.1-04.statement: The “Allow actions created by GitHub” setting admits Marketplace actions from verified creators.
github-actions-s4.1-04.explanation: GitHub-owned actions and Marketplace actions by verified creators have separate allow settings.
github-actions-s4.1-04.misconception: The GitHub-owned option includes all verified creators.

source.title: Disabling or limiting GitHub Actions for your organization

github-actions-s3.3-04.statement: Pushing a version tag to an action repository lists the action in GitHub Marketplace.
github-actions-s3.3-04.explanation: Maintainers publish an action in Marketplace by creating and publishing a release with the Marketplace option selected.
github-actions-s3.3-04.misconception: Tag creation alone publishes an action listing.

github-actions-s5.1-10.statement: `gh attestation verify` checks a binary's attestation against the repository given with `-R`.
github-actions-s5.1-10.explanation: GitHub CLI uses the artifact path and `-R OWNER/REPO` to verify the artifact attestation against its source repository.

source.title: Using artifact attestations to establish provenance for builds

github-actions-s3.2-01.statement: GitHub reads a custom action's metadata from `action.yaml` as well as `action.yml`.
github-actions-s3.2-01.explanation: A custom action uses `action.yml` or `action.yaml`; GitHub prefers `action.yml`.
